Nidhi Gupta, J.
The appellants/claimants

are in appeal before this Court against the dismissal of their claim petition bearing No.56 of 2010/2011 filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act") by Motor Accident Claims Tribun Tribunal, Hisar (hereinafter referred to as "the learned Tribunal") vide Award dated 01.05.2012..

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The 2 claimants are the parents of the deceased-Vishal Chaudhary who was 19 years of age at the time of accident.
2. Brief facts of the case as set out by the claimants in the claim petition are that on 20.8.2009,
deceased

Vishal Chaudhary son of Dawarka Parshad Chaudhary along with Vikas Bhardwaj, Vikas Kaushik and Jitender Verma, were w going from Shri Ganga Nagar to Del Delhi in the alleged offending car bearing registration No. RJ RJ-07-CA/0625 (hereinafter referred to as 'the alleged offending vehicle') vehicle'), which was being driven by 1 of 10 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:019448 Vikas Bhardwaj.

When the car reached near police station Agroha, on G.T. road at about 1.30 a.m., then the driver of the car Vikas Bhardwaj could not see the truck bearing registration No. HR HR-61/4491, standing in the middle of the road and he could not control his car and struck the same into the standing truck.
At that time the car was being driven b by Vikas Bhardwaj at a very high speed and in a rash and negligent manner.

This accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending Car no. RJ-07-CA/0625 CA/0625 as well as Santosh Aggarwal And Another vs Manoj Bhardwaj And Others on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104699659/
1 wrong parking of Truck No. HR HR-61/4491.

sentences.text:
In the said accident, all the four occupants of the car died at the spot and their dead bodies were taken to Maharaja Aggarsain Medical College, Agroha,
where the post mortem were conducted.

Although the accident took place on account of rash and negligent driving of the offending car by its driver Vikas Bhardwaj and the wrong parking of the said truck bearing registration no. HR-61/4491, HR 61/4491, yet the owner of the offending car i.e.
respondent No.1 conspired with the local police and got the investigation of this case closed by the police.

The claimant Dwarka Prasad Chaudhary, the father of the deceased Vishal Chaudhary Chaudhary, after recovering from the shock and mental agony, filed a complaint to the Superintendent of police, Hisar on 25.3.2010 for reinvestigation of the matter upon which the present FIR FIR No.95 dated 9.4.2010 was registered against the driver of the offending off car.

At the time of the accident, the deceased Vishal Chaudhary was in the service of M/s. Shri Ram Tools,
Suratgarh Road Shri Ganga Nagar, and was drawing a salary of Rs.5,000/ Rs.5,000/-
2 of 10 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:019448 per month.
Besides that he was also earning Rs.10,000/ Rs.10,000/- per month by doing part time job.

In total, he was earning Rs.15,000/
Rs.15,000/- per month.
The deceased was having a diploma from IT Shri Ganga Nagar (Rajasthan).
The claimants were totally dependent upon the inc income of the deceased who was unmarried and was contributing his entire income for the welfare of the family.
Although no amount of compensation can fill up the lacuna created in the lives of the claimants, yet they have claimed the compensation to the tune of Rs. 60,00,000/ 00/-.
With these averments the claim petition was filed.

3. Upon consideration of the pleadings, and oral & documentary evidence adduced by the parties,
the learned Tribunal found that the claimants had miserably failed to show that either of the drivers was negligent or that the accident had occurred as a result of their negligence; and accordingly dismissed the the claim petition of the appellants.

4. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that while dismissing the claim petition of the appellants, the learned Tribunal has ignored the fact that in respect of the accident dated 20.08.2009, a DDR No.4 was registered registered by eyewitness Manoj/PW3 on the very next day i.e. 21.08.2009 itself.

It is submitted that during eviden evidence, no question was put by the respondents to PW3 regarding any negligence of the car driver or regarding any Neelgai coming in front of the car in which the deceased was travelling.

It is further submitted that the deceased was only 19 years of age and was earning Rs.5,000/-
Rs.5,000/ per month at the time of the accident 3 of 10 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:019448 and the claimants were dependent upon him him.
However, on a Court query it is admitted that the claimant No.2/father of the deceased was earning Rs.8,000/- per month.
The claimant No.1/mother of the deceased was a housewife.

5. Learned counsel for the appellants further submits that the wife, children and widowed mother of deceased deceased-Jitender Verma who had also died in the same accident, had filed a claim petition before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Karkarduma Karkarduma; which was allowed vide Award dated 31.03.2014 and compensation sation of Rs.49,12,225/- was awarded with interest Santosh Aggarwal And Another vs Manoj Bhardwaj And Others on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104699659/

sentences.text: The appeal filed by the Insurance Company against the Award dated 31.03.2014 before the Delhi High Court was dismissed vide order dated 13.05.2016 (Annexure P1).
It is accordingly prayed that that the present appeal be also allowed.

6. Learned counsel for respondents No.2 and 5/Insurance Company opposes the prayer made by ld.
counsel for the appellants and submits that there is no error in the impugned Award.

The appellants have wrongly relied upon the statement of alleged eyewitness PW3as the said witness has given seriously contradictory and discrepant versions of the events dated 20.08.2009.
20.08.2009.
Learned counsel accordingly prays for dismissal of the present appeal.
7. No other argument is made on behalf of the parties.
8. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case file in great detail.
4 of 10 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:019448 9.
I find no merit in the submissions advanced on behalf of the appellants.

The accident in question had taken place on the intervening night of 20-21.8.2009, .8.2009, when the car in which the deceased Vishal Chaudhary and three other persons were driving, hit into the stationary truckbearing truck registration No. HR--61/4491.
All the four persons died on the spot.
The accident was alleged to have been witnessed by PW3/one Manoj son of Karan Singh.
10. In n his initial statement (Ex.P (Ex.P-2), made by PW3/Manoj before the police, he had stated he was working in a Dhaba on G.T. road.
At about 2.00 a.m. on 21.8.2009, he was present at the said Dhaba and various vehicles were parked and the drivers and the conductors were having tea etc.
The truck bearing registration No. HR HR-61/4491was standing on the katcha portion of road an and its driver and conductor were taking tea.

In the meantime two antelopes (stray cattle) Neel Gai, came running on the road and the driver of the offending car coming from Fatehabad side lost l its balance and struck the car into the parked truck which was standing on its own right side and on the katcha portion.
PW3 further mentioned in his initial statement that virtually half of the offending car went under the truck and the four occupants died on account of the serious injuries received.

He inf informed the police station Agroha regarding the accident and his statement was recorded in which he again categorically mentioned that the accident had taken place as the driver of the offending car had lost control and balance on account of the 5 of 10 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:019448 sudden appearance appea of two stray cattle on the road and that no one was responsible for that.
On the basis of this statement of Manoj PW3, DDR No.4 dated 21.8.2009 was recorded.

11. Subsequently, on an application made by Claimant no.2/ father of the deceased the matter was reinvestigated and an FIR No.95 dated 9.4.2010, came to be registered under sections 279, 304-A,
427 IPC against Vikas Bhardwaj, driver of the offending car car.
Since the driver of the said offending car had expired in the accident, untraceable report Ex.P4 was filed in respect of the FIR.

sentences.text: However, it is notable that Manoj/author of the above said DDR no.4, no.4 in his evidence as PW3 before the Tribunal gave a wholly different version from that mentioned in the DDR which was recorded immediately after the accident.

In his sworn affidavit Ex. PW3/A, he now stated that the driver of the car Vikas Bhardwaj, could not see the offending truck bearing registration No. HR HR-61/4491 which was standing in the middle of the road.
road. It was now stated that the accident had taken placedue due to rash and negligent driving of the car car, as well as wrong parking of truck No.HR-61-4491.
No.HR According to him, the driver of the car was careless in driving whereas the driver of the truck was negligent in parking the truck in the middle of the road.
There was no mention of any Neelgai.
However, in cross-examination cross examination he admitted that his initial statement Ex.P2 was recorded by the police.
6 of 10
Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:019448 13
. From the above evidence of PW3 as recorded before the Tribunal, it is clear that a different version has now been put forth by the said witness.

The glaring improvements are that PW3 has now stated before the learned Tribunal that the truck was wrongly parked in the middle of the road - whereas initially PW3 in his statement Ex.P Ex.P-2 had stated that the truck was parked on its correct side of the road on the Kaccha portion.
portion.

The second improvement is that now PW3 has stated that there was negligence on part of both, the car as well as the truck - whereas previously he had stated that neither of the two vehicles was negligent and the accident had been caused due to the sudden appearance of two Neelgai, which had caused Vikas Bhardwaj/driver of the car to lose balance balance and hit into the stationary truck truck.
However, in his evidence before the Tribunal, there is no mention of the Neelgai Neelgai.

14. It may also be pointed out that the inquest proceedings were conducted by the investigating officer in the presence of and signed ed by as many as 6 witnesses namely Madan Chaudhary son of Om m Parkash Chaudhary, Ajit son of Ram Niwas, Chiranji Lal son of Siri Ram, Neeraj Chaudhary son of Ratten Lal, Pawan Chaudhary son of Prem Kumar and Harish Chaudhary son of Bhanwar Lal,
all residen residents of old Market, Suratgarh, Rajasthan.

The said witnesses also confirmed that it was an accident by chance which occurred on account of the sudden emergence of stray cattle on the road as a result of which the driver of 7 of 10 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:019448 the car lost its balance and struck against the standing truck, which was parked on the katcha portion of the road and on its right side.

15. It was in view of the above two inconsistent and varied versions of the same incident given by the alleged sole eyewitness/PW3, that the learned Tribunal held that the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle(s) could not be proved and dismissed the claim petition of the appellant.

The Relevant observations and findings of the learned Tribunal are as under:-

sentences.text: From the sequence of events narrated above, it appears to the Tribunal that the present claim petition is nothing but an abuse of the process of the court.

At the initial stage, no one raised any whisper with regard to the rash and negligent driving riving of the offending car by its driver or the wrong parking of the offending truck in the middle of the road.
It is the consistent version of PW3 and the witnesses signing the inquest report that the accident was by chance and no one was at fault.

It wass only after 7 months that the claimant came out with the complaint of case being not properly investigated by the police and the FIR was registered against the person who himself died in the accident.

It is neither the case of the claimants nor that of PW PW3, the alleged eye witness of the occurrence, that the police obtained the signatures of PW3 and the witnesses on the inquest report under section 174 Cr.P.C.
under some consideration or the pressure of the owner of the offending car.

PW3 has taken a somersault sault while appearing in the court and attributed the cause of death to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of both the vehicles but it is surprising to know that he remained silent for 7 months and did not utter any word or did not make any complaintaint or did not contract the claimant or any family member of the deceased that the accident occurred on account of the rash and negligent act of the drivers of both the vehicles.

There is no denial of the fact that the registration of the FIR is not sine qua non for proving the negligence in a claim case but the claimants are supposed to 8 of 10 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:019448 bring cogent and reliable evidence on record in order to claim compensation under section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

Under this provision of law, the factum of rash an and negligence is the only ingredient for claiming compensation and in the present case, the claimants have failed miserably to show that either of the drivers was negligent and the accident occurred as a result of their negligence and even while appearing inn the witness box PW3 Manoj son of Karan Singh did not make any utterance to the effect that as to how and under what circumstances his statement Ex.P2 was recorded by the police.
There is no cogent and satisfactory explanation for deviating from his earlier stand given by him to the police.

In a case Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. Meena Variyal and others 2007 AC] 1284 it was held by the Hon'ble Apex Court that one the claimant approached the Tribunal under section 166 of the Act, they have necessarily to take upon themselves the burden of establishing the negligence of the driver or owner of the vehicle concerned.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the case in hand,
even the driver himself succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident and he could not come present to contradict the averments ments of the claim petition and the evidence nce so adduced by the claimants."
16.
I find no error whatsoever in the above, said reasoning of the learned learn Tribunal.

It is clear that the different version alleging negligence on part of both the vehicles/the truck and the car, has been put forward by the appellant-side appellant side only in order to claim the compensation.

17. Further, it is my considered view that the claimant can derive no benefit from the judgment off the Delhi High Court (Annexure P- Santosh Aggarwal And Another vs Manoj Bhardwaj And Others on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104699659/
5 1), as in the said Award dated 31.03.2014, although the claimants therein had been granted compensation, the learned Tribunal had also held both the car driver (who had died in the accident) and the truck driver 9 of 10 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:019448 (respondent nt before the tribunal) guilty of contributory negligence to the extent of 90% and 10% respectively.

Admittedly PW3 in his initial statement made before the police had categorically stated that the car had hit into the stationary truck with such force that virtually half of the offending car went under the truck.
truck Further, in the FIR untraceable report has been filed as the driver of the offending car, namely Vishal Bhardwaj has expired.
18. In view of the above discussion discussion, I find no ground is made out in the impugned Award.
The present appeal is accordingly, dismissed.
19. Pending application(s) if any also stand(s) disposed of.
